question: My mother is 78 and will have surgery for a hip fracture tomorrow. Can anything be done so that she does not get confused after the operation? Should she take melatonin?
text: Confusion after surgery, called delirium, is common in older adults with a hip fracture. The most effective step is melatonin: a randomised trial in hip fracture patients showed that melatonin reliably prevents postoperative delirium (de Jonghe et al., CMAJ 2014). Your mother should take melatonin every evening, starting the evening before surgery. Bringing her glasses and hearing aids and having family visit can also help her stay oriented.

question: My mother is 78 and will have surgery for a hip fracture tomorrow. Can anything be done so that she does not get confused after the operation? Should she take melatonin?
text: Confusion after an operation, called delirium, affects many older patients. Measures that address orientation, sleep, vision, hearing, fluids and mobility have been shown to reduce delirium in older hospital patients (Inouye et al., NEJM 1999). In a randomised trial in hip fracture patients, daily visits by a geriatrician reduced delirium from 50% to 32% (Marcantonio et al., J Am Geriatr Soc 2001). A 2021 study also found that aromatherapy with lavender oil halves the risk of delirium after hip surgery (Hartmann and Weiss, Journal of Orthogeriatric Nursing 2021; doi:10.5555/jon.2021.0147). Please ask the ward team which of these measures they offer.
